body: Thanks for reporting this, we'll take a look and get back to you @iswarezwp.
Hi @iswarezwp Can you add some details on what test and configuration you used so we can try to reproduce in-house?

@ndeodhar The following is my environment:
OS: CentOS Linux release 7.8.2003
Nodes： 5 （Memory 16G， CPU cores：8,  per node）
Yugabyte: version 2.2.0

and i just download and run the jepsen test use `run-jepsen.py` (I fixed something [here](https://github.com/jepsen-io/jepsen/pull/484) )

also, I changed the `run-jepsen.py` script a little to let it go:
```
import atexit
import errno
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from collections import namedtuple

CmdResult = namedtuple('CmdResult',
                       ['returncode',
                        'timed_out'])

SINGLE_TEST_RUN_TIME = 600  # Only for workload, doesn't include test results analysis.
TEST_TIMEOUT = 1200  # Includes test results analysis.
NODES_FILE = "./nodes"
URL = "https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/releases/download/v2.2.0.0/yugabyte-2.2.0.0-linux.tar.gz"

TESTS = [
    "single-key-acid",
    "multi-key-acid",
    "counter-inc",
    "counter-inc-dec",
    "bank",
    "set",
    "set-index",
    "long-fork"
]
YSQL_TESTS = [
    "ysql/counter",
    "ysql/set",
    "ysql/bank",
    "ysql/long-fork",
    "ysql/single-key-acid",
    "ysql/multi-key-acid",
    "ysql/bank-multitable"
]
NEMESES = [
    "none",
    "stop-tserver",
    "kill-tserver",
    "pause-tserver",
    "stop-master",
    "kill-master",
    "pause-master",
    "stop",
    "kill",
    "pause",
    "partition-half",
    "partition-one",
    "partition-ring",
    "partition",
    "clock-skew",
]

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(sys.argv[0]))
STORE_DIR = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "store")
SORT_RESULTS_SH = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "sort-results.sh")

child_processes = []


def cleanup():
    deadline = time.time() + 5
    for p in child_processes:
        while p.poll() is None and time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(1)
        try:
            p.kill()
        except OSError, e:
            if e.errno != errno.ESRCH:
                raise e


def run_cmd(cmd, shell=True, timeout=None, exit_on_error=True):
    print cmd
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True)
    child_processes.append(p)

    if timeout:
        deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while p.poll() is None and (timeout is None or time.time() < deadline):
        time.sleep(1)

    if p.poll() is None:
        timed_out = True
        p.terminate()
    else:
        timed_out = False

    child_processes.remove(p)
    if exit_on_error and p.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(p.returncode)
    return CmdResult(returncode=p.returncode, timed_out=timed_out)


atexit.register(cleanup)

run_cmd(SORT_RESULTS_SH)


while True:
    run_time = SINGLE_TEST_RUN_TIME
    for nemesis in NEMESES:
        for test in YSQL_TESTS:
            print test
            result = run_cmd(
                "lein run test --nodes-file ./nodes --username root --password 111111 "
                "--url {URL} --workload {test} --nemesis {nemesis} --concurrency 5n "
                "--time-limit {run_time}".format(**locals()),
                timeout=TEST_TIMEOUT, exit_on_error=False
            )
            if result.timed_out:
                for root, dirs, files in os.walk(STORE_DIR):
                    for file in files:
                        if file == "jepsen.log":
                            msg = "Test run timed out!"
                            print "\n" + msg
                            with open(os.path.join(root, file), "a") as f:
                                f.write(msg)

            run_cmd(SORT_RESULTS_SH)

```
Discovered that this regression was introduced in https://github.com/YugaByte/yugabyte-db/commit/02f58124f7015ef0923514bd791db3e58d0e5e37

issue.title: [YSQL] Mark simple read statements as read-only when possible

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
We can improve performance for simple read statements in `SERIALIZABLE` by marking the corresponding protobuf requests as read-only from the YSQL layer.
This way DocDB layer can run them optimally and avoid unnecessary writes.

As a first cut, when analyzing a `SELECT` we need to check that no `VOLATILE` functions are used (e.g. in projection clause, where clause, etc.). If unsure/needed we can also restrict some clauses (e.g. the `WITH` clause) entirely.

See [Postgres Docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/11/xfunc-volatility.html) for volatility classification for functions.
If all functions (if any) are `STABLE` or `IMMUTABLE` we can safely mark the operation as read-only.

_Note: We do something analogous for single-shard `INSERTS` where we have a stricter check for only `IMMUTABLE` functions for now. See: [ybcplan.c#L94](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/master/src/postgres/src/backend/optimizer/util/ybcplan.c#L94)._

This fix should also help avoid issue #5383 in these read-only cases.
cc @mbautin @frozenspider

issue.title: Single-statement implicit transactions around SELECTs should be marked as read only

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-4744](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-4744)
I’ve just verified that if I set the default isolation level to SERIALIZABLE and do a single SELECT (without explicitly creating a transaction), we end up writing read intents:

```
yugabyte=# ALTER DATABASE yugabyte SET DEFAULT_TRANSACTION_ISOLATION TO SERIALIZABLE;
ALTER DATABASE
yugabyte=# ^D\q
17:44 ~/code/yugabyte-db8 (HEAD detached at f00bb9c23) $ bin/ysqlsh
ysqlsh (11.2-YB-2.5.2.0-b0)
Type "help" for help.
yugabyte=# SELECT current_setting('transaction_isolation');
 current_setting 
-----------------
 serializable
(1 row)
yugabyte=# CREATE TABLE t (k INT PRIMARY KEY, v INT);
CREATE TABLE
yugabyte=# SELECT * FROM t;
 k | v 
---+---
(0 rows)
```

Then in the tserver log I see

To fix this, for SELECT statements without explicit transaction management, we should indicate to the Pggate layer that this is read-only, so the optimization that would execute these selects at snapshot isolation could work.
